Finally, the diagnosis of celiac disease is conﬁrmed by the response to a gluten free diet. Response may be documented clinically
(e.g., resolution of diarrhea, resumption of growth), in laboratory parameters (e.g., normalization of hemoglobin or iron status),
and histologically (restoration of normal histology in duodenal biopsies). The extent to which such resolution needs to be docu-
mented remains contextual. Prior to advent of serological tests, it was mandatory to document histological improvement in small
bowel biopsies on gluten withdrawal, and recurrence of changes upon gluten rechallenge. These measures are now considered
unnecessary in the majority of patients.
